A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same unified implicit-attention framework. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A-D support comparison despite retitling and reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original attention visualizations, segmentation and perturbation evaluations, component ablations, and Pascal VOC pseudo-label experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds ARC-E perturbation experiments and AMPLIFY in-context learning evaluations in Tables 2 and 5.

M1.justification: Section 3.1 extends the formulation to Mamba-2 using attention-head broadcasting and a diagonal normalization operator. The original Mamba, Griffin, RWKV, RetNet, and HGRN constructions remain, making this a localized extension.

E1.justification: v2 adds zero-shot ARC-E reasoning evaluation and few-shot in-context learning on Snarks, CommonsenseQA, and Formal Fallacies. Existing ImageNet, ImageNet-Segmentation, IMDB, and Pascal VOC coverage remains. These additions substantially broaden the evaluated tasks and scenarios.

E2.justification: New Table 5 compares the proposed attribution within AMPLIFY against vanilla Mamba and AMPLIFY using Ali et al. (2024) attribution. Existing comparator sets are retained; the ARC-E experiment reuses the earlier attribution comparator.

E3.justification: v2 introduces zero-shot activation/pruning evaluation of pretrained 1.3B and 2.8B Mamba models with AUAC/AU-MSE, plus a few-shot AMPLIFY protocol using a Mamba-790m proxy. These are substantial additional evaluation designs; the retained experiments are not reported as rerun under changed settings.

E4.justification: v2 adds activation/pruning analysis of attribution faithfulness in the zero-shot ARC-E setting. The component ablations in v1 Table 3/v2 Table 4, Figure 5, the RWKV gate analysis in Figure 6, and the qualitative IMDB cases remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests for its experiments. The added results continue the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Existing numerical tables and IMDB curves are retained, while Tables 2 and 5 add substantial results. For example, Table 5 reports 1.3B Snarks accuracy of 56.15% with the proposed AMPLIFY attribution versus 53.11% using Ali et al. attribution and 44.54% vanilla. Table 2 has conflicting metric directions and inconsistent model headers, limiting interpretation of individual ARC-E entries.

T1.justification: v2 adds headwise normalization statistics, the diagonal matrix N, and the Mamba-2 implicit-attention derivation in Equations 10-11. It also qualifies general linearization as a first-order approximation. Existing architecture derivations remain substantially unchanged.

C1.justification: The central unification and improved-explainability claims remain. v2 extends the framework's stated scope to Mamba-2 and broadens the introduction's downstream contribution from weakly supervised segmentation to attribution-based performance enhancement, including in-context learning.

C2.justification: v2 makes simplifications more explicit by qualifying generic linearization as a first-order approximation and stating that biases are ignored. It also interprets the new application results as demonstrating transfer of performance-enhancing techniques to gated RNNs. Existing vision and segmentation interpretations largely persist.

D1.justification: v1 Section 3.4's instructions for computing CLS attention with linear memory are removed. v2 newly specifies last-layer fine-tuning in Appendix C and identifies the Mamba-790m proxy and AMPLIFY protocol reference. Code and checkpoint links remain unchanged; the fine-tuning disclosure does not establish a changed experiment.

R1.justification: Hyena moves from a future-work mention to an explicitly acknowledged conceptual predecessor for composing data-controlled operators. v2 substantially develops novelty distinctions concerning purpose, included components, and interpretability. It also adds Zoology, Mamba-2, AMPLIFY, and evaluation references while removing several survey/application citations.

P1.justification: v2 changes the title and citation style, adds an experimental roadmap and Sections 4.1-4.3, reorders perturbation and segmentation discussions, and makes localized prose revisions. The overall section sequence and most existing method and appendix text remain recognizable.

P2.justification: v2 adds complete result tables for ARC-E and in-context learning, changes the document template, and reorganizes existing displays. Figure 2 is reduced beside text, and Figure 5 shares space with the compact ablation table. Existing figure images and plotted curves are retained.

improvement.justification: Table 5 adds useful controlled evidence that attribution choice can improve downstream in-context learning, extending v1's practical evidence beyond segmentation. The Hyena discussion also clarifies novelty. These gains are tempered by contradictory directions and model labels in Table 2 and removal of useful linear-memory implementation guidance; the existing empirical foundation remains unchanged.
